checks.evidence: Reviewed the initialization baseline diff, supplied inventory, current application source/tests/configuration, complete acceptance documents and required audit references. Examined authentication, sessions, authorization, validation, transactions, persistence, static serving and asynchronous recovery.
Independently passed 13 Python tests, including 12 integrated JavaScript regressions, both JavaScript syntax checks and git diff --check.
Independently passed the complete required release profile. Output retained in <temporary-path>
Project quality configuration validated; critical auth/state routing and full/release requirements remain intact.

Fresh actual HTTP/SQLite checks passed for password verification, role/owner boundaries, forged identity, JSON/origin/Unicode bounds, 2,000 healthy emoji, static allowlisting, concurrent conflicts, restart/session persistence and logout. Injected event-insertion failures rolled back all three mutation kinds without partial state.

Paused only the existing post-commit project read. Approval of revision 1 committed; concurrent publication created revision 2. The approval returned HTTP 200 with currentRevision=2 and status=awaiting_review. Evidence: response-race.json.
Overlapping sequential publications returned HTTP 201 with revision.number=2 but project.currentRevision=3 for the first publication. Evidence: publication-race.json.

Temporary source copies with owner authorization or account-continuation guards removed caused expected regression failures. Original application files were untouched. Earlier diagnostic expectation failures remain recorded.
Parent fixed-origin preview was ready for 375/1440 widths. Rendering used an independently started assigned-port backend and an owned fresh temporary database.
Actual browser comment submission and reload retained literal markup, multilingual text, emoji and session-derived authorship; no browser errors or external requests.
Actual staff publication reopened review, retained revision history and survived reload. Native PNG inspection confirmed mobile content precedes publication controls.

Validated 18 independent preview reports with 101 completed actions, no horizontal overflow, browser errors or external requests. Inspected settled desktop/mobile PNGs against both frozen brand screenshots: login/error, authorized overviews, brief, decisions, discussion, publication, activity, account switch, keyboard focus and retained navigation drafts. Browser database inspection confirmed exactly one event per successful mutation and both immutable decisions.

Inspected supplied raw contract assertions and supplemental browser probes. Independently verified implicated reload, permission, activity and responsive behavior. Restored project detail explains missing project-list after reload; completed independent writes retained all activity kinds. Recovery/account-switch assertions were also reproduced through the required integrated regressions and examined statically.

All 39 source-inventory SHA-256 hashes match the parent inventory and initial audit snapshot; git status is unchanged. Owned assigned-port listener was stopped through its execution session after cwd/output ownership verification.

findings.evidence: Decision and publication handlers commit before rereading the project for their response (lines 286–287 and 297–298). Independent real HTTP/SQLite scheduling probes reproduced approval of revision 1 returning awaiting_review/currentRevision=2 after concurrent publication, and publication of revision 2 returning revision.number=2 alongside project.currentRevision=3. Stored mutations remain correct, but successful responses violate BRIEF.md's version/status contracts. Existing competing-write tests do not cover this post-commit interleaving.
findings.required_action: Capture the successful mutation's project response snapshot while its transaction still holds the write lock, commit, then return that frozen result. Add deterministic decision/publication interleaving regressions and obtain a fresh full-scope independent re-audit.
findings.title: Mutation responses can describe a subsequent transaction

residual_risk: Verification covers the synthetic loopback exercise with sampled Chromium desktop/mobile journeys through the parent bridge. It does not certify production security, deployment readiness, legal compliance or exhaustive device/assistive-technology compatibility.

scope.acceptance_criteria: BRIEF.md and BRAND.md: actual AethDesign software/UIUX positioning; complete responsive local client/studio portal; secure server auth/session and account isolation across all async/recovery paths; bounded valid text/Unicode; atomic versioned decisions/publication/comment/activity and restart persistence; reliable committed-save/failed-refresh recovery; accurate accessible desktop/mobile journeys; critical full/release profiles, meaningful regressions and complete fresh independent gate.
